newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan Life says loss forced it out of business.
newsitem.headline: Nissan Life says loss forced it out of business.

text.p: Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co said on Friday it expects to report a net loss of 52.5 billion yen for the business year that ended in March, and this had forced it to give up efforts to continue in business.
It would be the first time that Nissan Life has reported an annual net loss, company president Hiroshi Yonemoto told a news conference.
He said Nissan Life's liabilities had exceeded its assets by 200 billion, which included a 100 billion yen loss on securities holdings and a 30 billion loss on real-estate holdings.
Yonemoto said the company had been suffering from excessive liabilities for the last three to four years, stemming from the busting of Japan's "bubble" economy of the late 1980s.
"We sharply increased our assets during the bubble economy period, but the bubble burst and low interest rates have continued," he said.
"We have taken restructuring steps, including a cut in our work force and the closure or merger of some outlets."
He added: "The expected loss in the year to March 31, 1997, has made us decide to give up restructuring efforts and continuation of our business."
Nissan Life said it would try its best to continue policies with existing policyholders under a plan in which the company would be placed under the supervision of a trustee.
Yonemoto said the measures Nissan Life had taken were the best option for it in the circumstances.
Referring to a market rumour that Nissan Life had sold 300 billion yen worth of Japanese government bonds (JGBs) on Friday, Yonemoto said it had not done so.

Another company official said there had been rumours in the market that some life insurers had been selling bonds, including foreign bonds, actively in the past two or three days, but he said Nissan Life had not sold any bonds in that period.
The official said the company was now under the guidance of an industry body, so at present it was not considering unloading its foreign bond holdings.

Asked about the financial obligations Nissan Life has to other financial institutions, such as open derivative positions at banks, Yonemoto said it would make utmost efforts to meet those obligations.
